text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Mubarak: Syria ready to listen but not to talk.
- U.S. Fox television network reported Islamic Jihad had planned this week to put a car bomb in Tel Aviv's Shalom Tower shopping and business centre.
- Major stake in Africa Israel will be sold to Israeli businessman Lev Leviev based on company value of about $400 million, sources close to negotiations said.

- Treasury checking proposal to raise companies tax to 40 percent from 36 percent and VAT to 19 percent from 17 percent, senior treasury source told Haaretz. A wide tax reform to be brought to government for approval at start of 1997, immediately after budget approved.
- Security establishment confirms: the Islamic Jihad planned an attack on Shalom Tower.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu says Palestinian entity to be established will be like Puerto Rico or Andorra.
- Detention without trial ordered against leader of outlawed Kach anti-Arab movement; steps against other Jewish extremists soon.
- Discussions begin on steps against Jewish extremists in Hebron.
- Africa Israel will be sold to Leviev.
